prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the passenger in a rear-end collision in League City, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1349; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just be called the passenger, but I'm happy to go on record.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were sitting and what the vehicle was doing when the collision happened?
A: I was in the front passenger seat. We had stopped at a light on the main road in League City, and then we got hit from behind.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?
A: Not really. I heard tires and then there was a jolt, and my head snapped back against the headrest.
Q: Did the driver of your vehicle have a chance to react?
A: Not that I could tell. It all happened in a second.
Q: After the collision, how did you feel physically?
A: My neck was stiff almost right away. By that evening my lower back had started to ache too, and it's gotten worse when I sit for long periods.
Q: Have you sought any medical treatment since the collision?
A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic the next day and then I've been seeing my family doctor for follow-up visits.
Q: Are you currently missing any work or limiting your daily activities?
A: I've had to take a few shifts off because lifting and driving for long stretches hurts. Simple things like cooking or sleeping through the night have been harder too.
Q: Did you have any neck or back problems before this collision?
A: No, nothing that needed treatment. I'd had normal aches now and then, but nothing like this.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I'm still going through physical therapy, and I hope to get back to normal as soon as I can.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
